- When sentiment is consistently 0.00, model tends to overestimate prices in early periods and underestimates in late periods — adjust forecast downward by 0.5–1.5% for late horizon days.
- After a price spike (e.g., >73.0), model often overshoots in the next 3–5 days — cap forecast at +1.5% above peak or use moving average of prior 5 days.
- If sentiment history shows a single non-zero value (e.g., 0.20), model may overreact to that signal — reduce forecast sensitivity by 20–30% for that period.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon — if forecast is >75.0, apply downward correction of 0.5–1.0% per day until price stabilizes.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is absent — add 0.3–0.7% to forecast for days with no sentiment signal, especially if price is trending upward.
- Forecast error is more pronounced in the first 5 days of the 30-day window — apply a 1–2% upward bias to early days if sentiment is flat.
